newsitem.title: USA: Loctite rejects Henkel's $1.2 billion offer.
newsitem.headline: Loctite rejects Henkel's $1.2 billion offer.

text.p: Loctite Corp. Monday rejected an unsolicited $1.19 billion offer from Germany's Henkel KGaA as inadequate and said it will recommend that its shareholders reject the bid.
The Hartford, Conn.-based chemicals and adhesives company said it has decided to seek buyers at a price that fully reflected its value.
Henkel, a chemicals and consumer products company that already owns 35 percent of Loctite, said it had no comment on Loctite's announcement.

"Our mission is to maximize stockholder value," said Robert Fiondella, chairman of a special committee of Loctite's board of directors. "We have instructed our advisors to respond to third-party inquiries, contact potential buyers and take all steps necessary to help achieve this goal."
Loctite said the committee's unanimous decision was based on the opinion of investment banker Dillon, Read & Co. Inc. and the state of the company's business and its long-term prospects.
The offer also failed to reflect adequately the significant range of potential benefits in a merger with Henkel, it said.

Earlier this month, Henkel launched a $56-a-share bid for the 65 percent of Loctite it does not already own, and raised the price to $57.75 a share a week later. The offer will remain open until Jan. 6, 1997, under an agreement the two companies made two years ago.

Dusseldorf, Germany-based Henkel, best known for its Persil laundry detergent, has said it wanted to enter into talks that would lead to a friendly takeover agreement, and if this failed, it would start a public tender offer.
Henkel's bid is valid only if enough shares are tendered to give it a controlling stake of more than 50 percent in Loctite.
Loctite makes engineered sealant, adhesives and lubricant products for the industrial, electronics, specialised medical, retail and professional automotive maintenance and repair markets.
Loctite's stock added 37.5 cents to $60.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
